maria: quick q — before i merge the client PR: need a final sanity check on embeddings contract for mixed inputs + truncation + batch limits. i wrote tests but want ops/infra/embeddings-owners to confirm behavior we expose to users. TL;DR: what do we accept in items, how do we truncate, and what do we return for empty/null items? maria: example payload we're validating:```json { \"model\": \"embed-1b\", \"items\": [\"short text\", 123, null, {\"html\": \"

a

\"}, \"very long text...\"] }``` jon: ok quick answers first-pass: we only guarantee string inputs. we coerce non-strings (numbers/objects) to their json-stringified form for backward compat, but mark this behavior as deprecated in the next major. null should be accepted as an item placeholder but we need to decide return semantics. derek: +1 to deprecate coercion. currently the backend pipeline calls to_string() on non-strings; i.e. 123 -> \"123\" and objects -> compact JSON. that is cheap to keep but messy for contract clarity. sophie: for truncation: we truncate by model tokenization window (model.max_tokens). truncation = trim tail (right-side) of the tokenized sequence by default. we SHOULD document that it's token-based, not byte/char. include an example snippet in docs. ryan: behavior on truncation: we compute the embedding on the truncated input, return normal vector. we do NOT return an error if an item is truncated. instead we add a warning in per-item metadata and emit a top-level warning for the request. maria: ok that answers most. specific ask: what if item becomes empty after truncation (e.g., user submits 10000 spaces or a very long single token stripped)? do we return null, zeros, or error? need deterministic behavior for client. jon: proposal from infra: return a zero vector (all 0.0) of the same dimensionality as model_dim for that model and set item.status = \"empty_after_truncation\" in the per-item metadata. rationale: avoids breaking numeric pipelines and preserves ordering. derek: caveat — returning zeros can be ambiguous vs a legitimately zero-like embedding. but in practice it's easier for downstream to handle. alternative is null + explicit error per item which forces breaking change. i'm +1 for zeros + metadata flag. sophie: also add a per-request header X-Embedding-Model-Dim so clients can allocate arrays before parsing. we already log model_dim in response metadata but header helps streaming clients. ryan: batch limits: current default max_items_per_request = 256 for hosted API. Dedicated/Dedicated+ can configure up to 2048 via tenant settings. if request > limit we return 413 with error_code = \"batch_too_large\" and a helpful message. we should add a clear link to quotas page. maria: what about combined token budget? e.g., 256 items each 20k tokens = insane. do we cap total tokens? jon: yes, we enforce a combined token budget keyed to model: default_total_token_limit = 1_000_000 tokens per request for hosted tier. Dedicated can raise. system checks tokenized_length_sum and fails fast with 413 + \"token_budget_exceeded\". we should include token counts in the error body for debugging. sophie: note on ordering: outputs must preserve input order 1:1. we MUST NOT reorder embeddings even if we batch internally. document that a response will be an array of vectors matching input positions; per-item metadata carries flags like \"truncated\" or \"empty_after_truncation\". maria: sample response example pls (short) so clients can adapt tests. embed-bot: automated snippet (from spec):```json { \"model\": \"embed-1b\", \"items\": [\"a\",\"b\",null], \"results\": [ {\"embedding\": [0.123, -0.02, ...], \"status\":\"ok\"}, {\"embedding\": [0.05, 0.001, ...], \"status\":\"ok\", \"truncated\":true}, {\"embedding\": [0.0, 0.0, ...], \"status\":\"empty_after_truncation\"} ], \"warnings\": [\"2 items truncated\"], \"model_dim\": \"1536\" }``` ryan: small impl detail: we'll return fixed-length arrays of floats as JSON numbers. for huge batches we stream newline-delimited JSON to reduce memory on client. keep that as opt-in header: Accept: application/x-ndjson. maria: perfect. decision notes i will add to the API spec PR: - accept and coerce non-strings (deprecated) - null allowed and preserved position - token-based truncation, truncate tail - if truncated -> embedding computed on truncated text, flagged per-item - if item empty after truncation -> zero vector + status flag - preserve ordering - max_items default 256 (hosted), 2048 configurable for Dedicated - combined token budget enforced jon: add unit tests: empty string -> zero vector; null -> zero vector? wait we need consistency: should raw null (client sent null) be treated same as empty string? derek: good catch. treat explicit null as \"empty input\" and return zero vector + status = \"empty_input\" (different from \"empty_after_truncation\"). update test matrix. sophie: i'll update docs and the openapi schema to include per-item status enum: [ok,truncated,empty_input,empty_after_truncation,failed]. maria: thanks all. i'll update client PR and spec, link the PR here when ready. ping me if you want different error codes/messages. ryan: thx — i'll add server-side telemetry for number of truncated items so we can surface common prompt truncation patterns. maria: linking PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/openapi/pull/422 (WIP) — will update tests once CI green. :bow:
